name: Quantum Volume
description: Quantum Volume is a hardware-agnostic metric developed by IBM to measure the capability of quantum computers. It uses random quantum circuits to test the combination of qubit count, gate fidelity, connectivity, and error rates. Quantum Volume provides a single-number metric that captures overall quantum processor performance and has become an industry-standard benchmark.
significance: The de facto industry standard for comparing quantum processors, capturing the interplay of qubit count, gate fidelity, connectivity, and error rates.

news.title: Sandia, Quantinuum, and NVIDIA Introduce QUOPS Framework, Finds Quantum Hardware 100,000× Below Practical Utility
news.excerpt: A Sandia National Laboratories-led team introduced the Quantum Universal Operations Performance System (QUOPS), an architecture-agnostic metric benchmarking the largest circuits a processor can execute successfully and how quickly. Testing Google Willow (Q=216), IBM ibm_boston (Q=204), Quantinuum H2-1 (Q=1,320) and Helios-1 (Q=1,504), the study finds current hardware must improve ~100,000-fold in computational capability to reach examined scientific workloads.

news.title: Quantum Computers Need 100,000-Fold Performance Gain For Scientific Utility, Study Finds
news.excerpt: Benchmarking study by Sandia, Quantinuum, NVIDIA and partner labs introduces QUOPS as a cross-platform metric and measures processors from Google, IBM, and Quantinuum. Quantinuum's Helios-1 reached 1,504 QUOPS — the highest physical score — while Google Willow and IBM ibm_boston reached 216 and 204 QUOPS respectively. The paper concludes current systems fall five orders of magnitude short of the capability needed to solve recognised scientific problems.
